summary:
Remora : Lost in Space, Never Lost in History 
Remora is an educational app designed to commemorate the abandoned missions of NASA. Our primary aim is to teach younger generations the stories of these missions in a way that leaves an indelible impact in their memories through a personalized experience.We focused on making the app simple to use while providing a great amount of immersion to encourage students to learn more and be eager to complete all the missions. The app workflow is as follows: 1- Registration and Avatar creation. 2- mission selection via AR card scanning. 3- the mission begins by interactive storytelling. 4- then we give them interactive quizzes regarding the mission before they head to the next mission. We intend to work on linking the app content to educational cirricula through showing the impact of different physics phenomena on the spaceship and test their understanding by a final original mission where they compose their own spaceship and take off to their own mission.
details:
Project Overview: Remora — Lost in Space, Never Lost in History

1. What does it do & How does it work?

Remora ("Lost in space, never lost in history") is an immersive, web-based educational adventure designed for elementary and school students to explore historic and discarded NASA equipment—such as landers, rovers, orbiters, and experiment packages—left behind on the Moon and Mars.

The Journey & Mission Control: Users start by entering their name and choosing a personalized astronaut avatar, which acts as a consistent Mission Control companion that greets them by voice, reacts to milestones, guides exploration, and personalizes prompts throughout the experience.

Exploration & AR Sky Hunt: Users enter a cinematic space dashboard showing Earth and the surrounding space, where they can navigate using hand motions or controls. They scan circular NASA mission cards with QR codes that open the device camera to trigger an Augmented Reality (AR)—or 3D fallback—environment, allowing students to sweep the real sky with their phones to track down and unlock specific lost spacecraft.

Interactive Physics & Telemetry Challenges: Once a machine is discovered, users unlock multi-chapter interactive stories narrated with text-to-speech support detailing its history, active lifespan, and why it stopped. Clicking on specific onboard tools (such as sensors) launches simple animated explanations of the underlying physics, paired with real NASA-data orbital puzzles and telemetry challenges (e.g., adjusting target altitude) featuring safe-failure feedback.

Beyond the Screen & Gamification: Completed missions feature fun physics quizzes, adaptive concept explanations, creative student feedback loops (allowing users to pitch alternative reuse ideas for abandoned machinery), and hands-on offline activities including Physics & Aerodynamics Labs (home experiments using everyday items) and DIY Rover Prototyping (building miniature rovers from cardboard and modular parts). Every completed spacecraft unlocks forever in the student's personal Virtual Space Museum ("Discovery Archive"), rewarding badges, achievements, and a verified, personalized Junior Astronaut Certificate of Mission Success.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

Transforming Learning: The application transforms complex, traditional space history and physics into an engaging, accessible hunt that students and teens genuinely want to play.

Low-Cost & Classroom Scalable: Designed using accessible paper cards, smartphones, and household items to build physical DIY cardboard rovers at home, Remora is built on open NASA data so it can be easily scaled to any classroom.

Fostering STEM Curiosity: By shifting away from dry textbooks and combining digital exploration with hands-on prototyping, it nurtures curiosity, critical thinking, and a lifelong interest in STEM fields while maintaining strict historical accuracy.

3. Development Tools and Technologies

Built as an interactive web application.

Utilized an antigravity application framework for the prototype development.

Integrated Augmented Reality (AR) sky-tracking camera features, QR code scanning, interactive telemetry simulations, and text-to-speech narration capabilities.

4. Creativity & Innovation

Remora bridges the gap between entertainment, digital exploration, and physical hands-on learning. Instead of passive reading, students actively hunt for abandoned NASA machinery through AR, solve safe-failure orbital telemetry puzzles, interact with component-level physics animations, build physical DIY cardboard rovers at home, and contribute their own creative ideas for repurposing historic space hardware.

5. Key Design Factors Considered

Mobile-First Responsiveness: Optimized for seamless performance across smartphones and devices.

Child-Friendly Accessibility: Features high contrast, clear navigation, and audio captions to support young learners.

Brand & Visual Immersion: Strict adherence to NASA branding guidelines coupled with a permanent cinematic space background to maintain complete visual immersion.

Disclaimer: these are the functions intended for the full application but the prototype has only the functions time allowed us to implement.
